text:
Zach Hyman is back with Edmonton after a spell on injured reserve; the Oilers activated him on November 7 and he picked up an assist in his first game back against Vancouver. He's played only eight games, and the start has been quiet: one goal, two points, 6.7% shooting.

We wouldn't read much into that. The chances are still coming. He's at 0.96 expected goals per 60 of his own, and our numbers expected nearly five points from his minutes, not two. Hyman has made a career out of scoring from the paint, and those goals tend to arrive in bunches once a player is healthy and back beside the top guys.

The bigger question is age. He's 34, and his own chance rate is down from 1.82 per 60 last season. Evolving-Hockey still had him driving play at the 98th percentile of forwards in 2025-26, with very good linemates helping. Our range has him around 24 goals and 49 points from here, if he stays in the lineup. Watch whether he gets his net-front spot on the top power play back.
headline: Zach Hyman is back and still looking for his touch
